BillHeading.BriefDescription: Protecting children from imminent risk of harm.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to protecting children from imminent risk of harm; and amending RCW 26.44.050.

BillSection.BillSectionHeader: Sec. 1. RCW 26.44.050 and 2024 c 328 s 105 are each amended to read as follows:Abuse or neglect of child—Duty of law enforcement agency or department of children, youth, and families—Taking child into custody without court order, when.
BillSection.P: (1) Except as provided in RCW 26.44.030(12), upon the receipt of a report alleging that abuse or neglect has occurred, the law enforcement agency or the department must investigate and provide the protective services section with a report in accordance with chapter 74.13 RCW, and where necessary to refer such report to the court.

(2)(a) A law enforcement officer may take, or cause to be taken, a child into custody without a court order if there is probable cause to believe that taking the child into custody is necessary to prevent imminent physical harm to the child due to child abuse or neglect, including that which results from sexual abuse, sexual exploitation, a high-potency synthetic opioid, or a pattern of severe neglect, and the child would be seriously injured or could not be taken into custody if it were necessary to first obtain a court order pursuant to RCW 13.34.050. The law enforcement agency or the department investigating such a report is hereby authorized to photograph such a child for the purpose of providing documentary evidence of the physical condition of the child.

P.TextRun: (b) Law enforcement shall immediately take a child into custody when it receives a report from the department pursuant to subsection (3) of this section.

(3) The department shall immediately notify law enforcement when there is probable cause to believe that taking the child into custody is necessary to prevent imminent physical harm to the child due to child abuse or neglect, including that which results from sexual abuse, sexual exploitation, a high-potency synthetic opioid, or a pattern of severe neglect, and the child would be seriously injured or could not be taken into custody if it were necessary to first obtain a court order pursuant to RCW 13.34.050. Evidence of imminent physical harm includes the department's belief that a child's home is unsafe to enter.
